test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: On 8–9 November 2025, the Ministry of Home Affairs and the National Judicial Academy hosted a national conference in Bhopal focusing on which area?
solution:
The correct answer is __**New Criminal Laws**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **8–9 November**, the **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** and the **National Judicial Academy (NJA)** organized a national conference in **Bhopal**, **Madhya Pradesh**, dedicated to the implementation and nuances of the **New Criminal Laws**.
 
• The conference served as a critical platform for members of the **judiciary**, **legal experts**, and **administrative officials** to discuss the transition from colonial-era statutes to a more modern, **citizen-centric** legal framework.
 
• The primary focus was on the three transformative acts: the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)**, the **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)**, and the **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA)**.
 
• Discussions highlighted the shift from a "punishment-based" system to a "justice-based" system, emphasizing the **decolonization** of the Indian **criminal justice system**.
 
• The event underscored the importance of **technological integration**, such as the mandatory **videography** of crime scenes and the use of **digital evidence**, which are core components of the new legal reforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023**:
 
 
• It replaces the **Indian Penal Code (IPC)** of **1860**.
 
• It introduces **community service** as a form of punishment for specific petty offenses and defines **terrorism** and **organized crime** for the first time within a general criminal code.
 
 
 
• **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023**:
 
 
• It replaces the **Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)** of **1973**.
 
• It mandates **strict timelines** for **investigations**, **trials**, and the delivery of **judgments**, aiming to reduce the massive backlog of cases in Indian courts.
 
 
 
• **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023**:
 
 
• It replaces the **Indian Evidence Act** of **1872**.
 
• It expands the definition of **documentary evidence** to include **electronic or digital records**, giving them the same legal standing as paper documents.
 
 
 
• The implementation of these laws officially began on **July 1, 2024**, marking a significant milestone in India's **legislative history**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Judicial Academy (NJA)**: Located in **Bhopal**, it is a premier institute for the **training** and **capacity building** of judges across India. Its role in this conference was to ensure the **judiciary** is well-equipped to interpret the **new statutes** correctly.
 
• **Decolonization Objective**: A major theme of the conference was removing the **colonial mindset** embedded in the old laws (which were drafted by the **British**) and replacing them with laws that reflect **contemporary Indian values**.
 
• **Victim Rights**: The new laws grant more rights to **victims**, including the right to be **informed** about the progress of an investigation within **90 days**.
 
• **Zero FIR**: The **BNSS** formally institutionalizes the concept of **Zero FIR**, allowing any person to file a **First Information Report** at any police station, regardless of the **jurisdiction** where the crime occurred.
